key_reasoning.reason: Five components in one subsystem (src/mcp): callback-server (typed CallbackTimeoutError/OAuthCallbackError, sanitized and escaped callback page, security headers), mcp-oauth-provider (hints, refresh-rotation adoption, retry), token-store (read-only peek, conditional forget), auth-lock (per-lock stale age), constants (new getMcpAuthTimings abstraction deriving all timings from one env var).

Closest existing pattern is the already-shipped persisted login and auth lock, which does not cover the new security-sensitive parts: HTML-escaping and control-char stripping of untrusted callback text, and refresh-token rotation races between proxy processes with no cross-process lock (last writer wins). Credential handling is involved, but the change hardens existing behavior and is reversible. Bumped to L, not XL.
15 files per diffstat (XL band 11-15): 5 source, 1 doc, 9 test files (helper plus 8 suites). About 60% of the files are tests, so effective production churn is lower than the score suggests.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk: security-sensitive work (untrusted callback text sanitization/escaping, persisted refresh-token handling) reflected in L score
Technical Risk: enumerated edge/error cases (timeout, oauth error, rotation, lock staleness) each backed by new dedicated test suites
